Container.Name: tunnelbunny
Container.Overview:
Is my traffic in the VPN tunnel, is DNS leaking, and how fast is it?
Tunnel Bunny answers those three questions from the network it sits on. Put it on a VLAN, or borrow another container's network namespace with --net=container:name, and it measures from exactly that position without touching the container you are debugging.
The VPN and DNS verdicts are based on YOUR provider, not on your ISP: set VPN Provider to a pattern matching the ASN/org of your exit, and every resolver seen is checked against it. With nothing set the measurement is shown but no verdict is claimed. Several providers register under a different company name - Mullvad's network is "31173 Services AB", NordVPN appears as both Tefincom and PacketHub - so the web UI ships a list, and after a run it offers the name it actually saw.
Click WebUI for the page, or open Console and run: check (vpn|dns|speed|all). The image also ships curl, dig, mtr, ping and Ookla's speedtest, so it doubles as a shell to debug from.

Config.Name: VPN Provider
Config.Description: Regex matched against the ASN/org field of your exit IP. Leave empty and set it from the web UI, which ships a list of common providers. Examples: Mullvad = 31173 Services|Mullvad, NordVPN = Tefincom|PacketHub|NordVPN, Proton = Proton, OVPN = Obehosting|OVPN. Left empty, the measurement is shown but no verdict is given.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Stores the VPN provider set from the web UI. Without it the setting is lost when the container is re-created.
